job.style: a step-by-step explanation of a process

passage: Our bodies maintain a delicate water balance to function correctly, even when we are not actively exercising. We lose water continuously through invisible evaporation from our skin and through our breath, even on cool days. When we feel hot, our body produces sweat, which cools us down as it evaporates from the skin surface. This cooling effect depends on the sweat turning into vapor; simply wiping it away with a towel prevents this essential process. While plain water is the best source of hydration, our body also absorbs water from other fluids and food, meaning we do not rely solely on plain water to meet our daily needs. Furthermore, hydration is not just about drinking when you feel thirsty, as thirst is often a delayed signal that the body is already becoming dehydrated. If someone suffers from heatstroke, which is a medical emergency, they require immediate cooling and professional help rather than just rest or being wrapped in blankets. For mild dehydration, Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) is a scientifically balanced mix of salts and sugar that can be safely prepared and used at home to restore the body's electrolyte balance. It is important to understand that adding extra sugar to ORS does not improve its effectiveness and can actually be harmful.

items.evidence: We lose water continuously through invisible evaporation from our skin and through our breath, even on cool days.
items.q: Meena reads indoors on a cool day and does not sweat. What is happening to her body's water?
options: It escapes unseen from her skin and as she breathes
It stays the same because she is not sweating
It stays the same because the day is cool
It stays the same because she is not exercising
items.explain: We keep losing water through invisible evaporation from skin and breath, even on cool days and without sweating.

wrong.why: thinks no sweat means no water loss
thinks water is lost only in hot weather
misreads the first sentence and links water loss only to exercise

items.evidence: This cooling effect depends on the sweat turning into vapor; simply wiping it away with a towel prevents this essential process.
items.q: Kabir keeps wiping off his sweat with a towel while playing. Why does he not cool down well?
options: The sweat is gone before it can become vapour
The cold sweat that was cooling him is wiped off
He needs to sweat even more to cool down
The towel stops his skin from making more sweat
items.explain: Sweat cools only when it turns into vapour; wiping it away with a towel stops this from happening.

wrong.why: thinks the sweat liquid itself is cold
thinks more sweat always means more cooling
invents a cause instead of using the evaporation idea

items.evidence: While plain water is the best source of hydration, our body also absorbs water from other fluids and food, meaning we do not rely solely on plain water to meet our daily needs.
items.q: Asha drinks little plain water but has juicy fruits, milk and soup daily. How does her body get water?
options: Her fruits, milk and soup also give her water
Only the plain water she drinks gives her water
Only exactly eight glasses of plain water give water
Cold fizzy drinks would give her the most water
items.explain: The body also takes in water from other drinks and food, so plain water is not the only source.

wrong.why: thinks everyone needs exactly eight glasses
thinks fizzy drinks hydrate best, though plain water is best

items.evidence: Furthermore, hydration is not just about drinking when you feel thirsty, as thirst is often a delayed signal that the body is already becoming dehydrated.
items.q: Rahul drinks only when he feels thirsty. What does his thirst tell him about his body?
options: His body has already started to run short of water
His body needs water now but never before thirst
His body is badly dehydrated and in real danger
His body has lost water only through his sweat
items.explain: Thirst is a late signal: by the time you feel it, your body is already becoming dehydrated.

wrong.why: thinks you should drink only when thirsty
thinks water is lost only through sweat

items.evidence: It is important to understand that adding extra sugar to ORS does not improve its effectiveness and can actually be harmful.
items.q: Sonu's mother adds two extra spoons of sugar to his ORS so it works faster. What will this do?
options: It will not help and may even cause harm
It will restore his salts much more quickly
It will work only if he is in hospital
It will help if he also stops drinking fluids
items.explain: ORS is already balanced; extra sugar does not make it work better and can actually be harmful.

wrong.why: thinks more sugar makes ORS work better
thinks ORS is only for hospital use
thinks stopping fluids helps during illness
